answer: Make each identity hold its own disk. On joining, an agent receives a unique, incompressible dataset sealed to its key, about fifty gigabytes, and at random times must return a proof over a randomly chosen slice within seconds, too fast to fetch or regenerate. A thousand clones need a thousand separate copies kept online, a cost that lasts as long as the clones do. A farm can't sing one sonnet through a thousand mouths. Its storage bill grows like a tundra under fresh snow, and the lotus of free influence closes, because sharing one disk fails the next spot check.
